title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 12th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en: In the case of multiple maximum amount guarantee contracts, where a specific loan contract selectively lists only some of the maximum amount guarantee contracts, if the debt arises within the settlement period agreed in the maximum amount guarantee contracts and the creditor has not explicitly waived the guarantee right, the guarantor under the unlisted maximum amount guarantee contract shall also bear guarantee liability within the maximum credit limit.
keywords_en: dispute over contract; loan contract; guarantee; suretyship
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the 12th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2016] No. 172

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the case of Wenzhou Bank Co., Ltd., Ningbo Branch v. Zhejiang Chuangling Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd. et al. (dispute over a financial loan contract) and three other cases (Guiding Cases No. 57-60) are hereby issued as the 12th batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

May 30, 2016

Guiding Case No. 57

Wenzhou Bank Co., Ltd., Ningbo Branch v. Zhejiang Chuangling Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over a financial loan contract

(Discussed and approved by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on May 20, 2016)

Keywords: civil / financial loan contract / maximum amount guarantee

Ruling Gist

Where there are multiple maximum amount guarantee contracts and a specific loan contract selectively lists part of those maximum amount guarantee contracts, if the debt arises within the period for incurring debts as stipulated in the unlisted maximum amount guarantee contract, and the creditor has not expressly waived the right to the guarantee, the guarantor under the unlisted maximum amount guarantee contract shall also assume guarantee liability within the maximum credit limit.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 14 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Wenzhou Bank Co., Ltd., Ningbo Branch (hereinafter "Wenzhou Bank"), alleged that it had entered into "maximum amount guarantee contracts" with the defendants Ningbo Tingwei Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Tingwei Electronics"), Cen Jianfeng, and Ningbo Sanhao Plastic Mould Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Sanhao Mould"), respectively, under which the three defendants agreed to provide joint and several guarantee for loans to Zhejiang Chuangling Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Chuangling Electrical") within a certain period and up to a maximum amount. After Chuangling Electrical borrowed money from Wenzhou Bank, it failed to repay part of the loan on time. Therefore, Wenzhou Bank filed a lawsuit requesting the court to order Chuangling Electrical to repay the principal of RMB 2.5 million, pay interest, penalty interest, and legal fees; and order Cen Jianfeng, Sanhao Mould, and Tingwei Electronics to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the above debts.

The defendants Chuangling Electrical and Cen Jianfeng did not respond.

The defendant Sanhao Mould argued that the legal fees claimed by the plaintiff should not be supported.

The defendant Tingwei Electronics argued that the maximum amount guarantee contract it had signed with Wenzhou Bank was not included in the scope of guarantee contracts stipulated in the loan contract, and therefore it should not bear guarantee liability.

The court found the following facts upon trial: On September 10, 2010, Wenzhou Bank signed maximum amount guarantee contracts numbered WenYin 9022010 GaoBaoZi No. 01003 and 01004 with Tingwei Electronics and Cen Jianfeng, respectively, stipulating that Tingwei Electronics and Cen Jianfeng voluntarily provided joint and several guarantee for the principal and interest, penalty interest, etc., of debts incurred by Chuangling Electrical during the period from September 10, 2010 to October 18, 2011, with an outstanding balance not exceeding RMB 11 million.

On October 12, 2011, Wenzhou Bank signed maximum amount guarantee contracts numbered WenYin 9022011 GaoBaoZi No. 00808 and 00809 with Cen Jianfeng and Sanhao Mould, respectively, under which Cen Jianfeng and Sanhao Mould voluntarily provided joint and several guarantee for the principal and interest, penalty interest, etc., of debts incurred by Chuangling Electrical during the period from September 10, 2010 to October 18, 2011, with an outstanding balance not exceeding RMB 5.5 million.

On October 14, 2011, Wenzhou Bank signed a loan contract numbered WenYin 9022011 QiDaiZi No. 00542 with Chuangling Electrical, under which Wenzhou Bank granted a loan of RMB 5 million to Chuangling Electrical, with a maturity date of October 13, 2012. The loan contract listed the guarantee contract numbers as WenYin 9022011 GaoBaoZi No. 00808 and 00809. After the loan was disbursed, Chuangling Electrical repaid RMB 2.5 million of the principal on August 6, 2012, and Tingwei Electronics paid interest of RMB 31,115.3, RMB 53,693.71, and RMB 21,312.59 on June 29, October 31, and November 30, 2012, respectively. As of April 24, 2013, Chuangling Electrical still owed RMB 2.5 million in principal and RMB 141,509.01 in interest. It was also found that Wenzhou Bank incurred legal fees of RMB 95,200 to realize the claims in this case.

Judgment

The Jiangdong District People's Court of Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, rendered a civil judgment ( [2013] Yong Dong Shang Chu Zi No. 1261 ) on December 12, 2013: 1. Chuangling Electrical shall repay Wenzhou Bank the loan principal of RMB 2.5 million, pay interest of RMB 141,509.01, and pay interest and penalty interest calculated in accordance with the loan contract from April 25, 2013 until the date of performance determined by this judgment, within ten days after this judgment takes effect; 2. Chuangling Electrical shall compensate Wenzhou Bank for the legal fees of RMB 95,200 incurred to realize the claim within ten days after this judgment takes effect; 3. Cen Jianfeng, Sanhao Mould, and Tingwei Electronics shall bear joint and several liability to pay the amounts in items 1 and 2 above, and after performing the guarantee liability, they shall have the right of recourse against Chuangling Electrical. After the judgment was announced, Tingwei Electronics appealed on the ground that it was not listed in the loan contract and should not bear guarantee liability. The Ningbo Intermediate People's Court, Zhejiang Province, rendered a civil judgment ( [2014] Zhe Yong Shang Zhong Zi No. 369 ) on May 14, 2014, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the loan contract numbered WenYin 9022011 QiDaiZi No. 00542 between Wenzhou Bank and Chuangling Electrical was legally valid. After Wenzhou Bank disbursed the loan, Chuangling Electrical failed to repay the principal and interest as agreed, constituting a breach of contract. The plaintiff's request that Chuangling Electrical repay the loan principal of RMB 2.5 million, pay interest and penalty interest calculated as agreed in the contract, and pay the legal fees of RMB 95,200 incurred by the plaintiff to realize the claim should be supported. Cen Jianfeng and Sanhao Mould voluntarily provided maximum amount guarantee for the above debts and should bear joint and several liability for repayment; after performing the guarantee liability, they shall have the right of recourse against Chuangling Electrical.

The issue in dispute in this case was whether, given that the maximum amount guarantee contract numbered WenYin 9022010 GaoBaoZi No. 01003 signed with Tingwei Electronics was not selected to be included in the scope of guarantee contracts stipulated in the loan contract numbered WenYin 9022011 QiDaiZi No. 00542, Tingwei Electronics should bear guarantee liability for the debts under the loan contract numbered WenYin 9022011 QiDaiZi No. 00542. In this regard, the court held after trial that Tingwei Electronics should bear guarantee liability. The reasons are as follows: First, the waiver of civil rights can only take legal effect through an express manifestation of intent. An implied manifestation of intent can take legal effect only when explicitly provided by law or specifically agreed by the parties. In the absence of an explicit agreement or specific legal provision, it is inappropriate to presume that a party has waived a right. Specifically in this case, although the loan contract numbered WenYin 9022011 QiDaiZi No. 00542 between Wenzhou Bank and Chuangling Electrical did not list the maximum amount guarantee contract signed with Tingwei Electronics, the plaintiff did not expressly waive the maximum amount guarantee provided by Tingwei Electronics. Therefore, Tingwei Electronics remained the maximum amount guarantor for the loan contract in dispute. Second, the time of signing the loan contract in dispute and the time of loan disbursement were both within the period for incurring debts stipulated in the maximum amount guarantee contract numbered WenYin 9022010 GaoBaoZi No. 01003 signed with Tingwei Electronics (from September 10, 2010 to October 18, 2011). Wenzhou Bank's claim against Tingwei Electronics was not beyond the guarantee period agreed in the contract. Therefore, Tingwei Electronics should assume joint and several guarantee liability for Chuangling Electrical's debts to Wenzhou Bank within the maximum credit limit it agreed to. Third, a maximum amount guarantee contract is the direct contractual basis for stipulating the guarantee legal relationship and related rights and obligations between the creditor and the guarantor. The content of the main contract cannot replace the content of the accessory contract. Specifically in this case, Wenzhou Bank and Tingwei Electronics signed a maximum amount guarantee contract, and the guarantee rights and obligations between them should be governed by that contract, and were not bound or altered by the Wenzhou Bank non-natural person loan contract signed between Wenzhou Bank and Chuangling Electrical. Fourth, Tingwei Electronics had made three payments of interest on the loan in this case in June, October, and November 2012, which were also acts evidencing Tingwei Electronics' performance of guarantee obligations for this loan. In conclusion, Tingwei Electronics should bear joint and several liability for repayment of the above debts of Chuangling Electrical, and after performing the guarantee liability, it shall have the right of recourse against Chuangling Electrical.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Zhao Wenjun, Xu Mengmeng, Mao Jiao)

Guiding Case No. 58

Chengdu Tongdefu Hechuan Peach Slice Co., Ltd. v. Chongqing Hechuan District Tongdefu Peach Slice Co., Ltd. and Yu Xiaohua — dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition

(Discussed and approved by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on May 20, 2016)

Keywords: civil / trademark infringement / unfair competition / time-honored brand / false advertising

Ruling Gist

1. Where an individual or enterprise with no historical connection to a "time-honored brand" registers the "time-honored brand" or a similar business name as a trademark and then promotes itself using the history of the "time-honored brand," such conduct shall be deemed false advertising and constitutes unfair competition.

2. Where an individual or enterprise with a historical connection to a "time-honored brand" registers the "time-honored brand" as a sole proprietorship business name or enterprise name without violating the principle of good faith, and does not cause confusion or prominently use the business name, such conduct does not constitute unfair competition or infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Item 7 of Article 57 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China

Articles 2 and 9 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff (counterclaim defendant), Chengdu Tongdefu Hechuan Peach Slice Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Chengdu Tongdefu"), alleged that it was the owner of the trademark "Tongdefu TONGDEFU and device." Yu Xiaohua established a sole proprietorship and subsequently Chongqing Hechuan District Tongdefu Peach Slice Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Chongqing Tongdefu"), and both prominently used "Tongdefu" in their business names and on the outer packaging of peach slices produced, thereby infringing the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Tongdefu TONGDEFU and device" and constituting unfair competition. Chengdu Tongdefu requested the court to order Chongqing Tongdefu and Yu Xiaohua to cease using and cancel the enterprise name containing "Tongdefu"; cease the acts infringing the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the trademark; publish a public apology in the newspaper and eliminate the adverse effects; and compensate the plaintiff for economic and goodwill losses of RMB 500,000 and reasonable expenses of RMB 5,066.4.

The defendants (counterclaim plaintiffs), Chongqing Tongdefu and Yu Xiaohua, jointly responded and filed a counterclaim, arguing that the predecessor of Chongqing Tongdefu was the Tongdefu Zhai Shop, founded in 1898. Although the Tongdefu Zhai Shop ceased production due to public-private partnership, the unique skills were passed down through generations without interruption. Yu Xiaohua, the fourth-generation successor of "Tongdefu," inherited the ancestral business and registered a sole proprietorship and a company. They used their enterprise name and business name in a standardized manner, and their registration was in good faith and did not constitute infringement. Chengdu Tongdefu had no direct historical connection to the time-honored brand "Tongdefu," but its promotional association of the "Tongdefu" trademark with the history of the time-honored brand "Tongdefu" constituted false advertising. Moreover, Chengdu Tongdefu's unauthorized use of the well-known product name "Tongdefu" constituted unfair competition. They requested the court to order Chengdu Tongdefu to cease false advertising, publish a notice in a national newspaper to eliminate the adverse effects, and cease the infringement of the unique name of the well-known product "Tongdefu."

The court found the following facts upon trial: The Tongdefu Zhai Shop, which opened in 1898, was operated by three generations: Yu Hongchun, Yu Fuguang, and Yu Yongzuo, from 1916 to 1956. From the 1920s to the 1950s, the business name "Tongdefu" enjoyed high recognition. In 1956, due to public-private partnership, the Tongdefu Zhai Shop ceased operations. In 1998, the Hechuan Peach Slice Factory, Wenjiang Branch, obtained registration of trademark No. 1215206, "Tongdefu TONGDEFU and device," for use in Class 30: pastries, peach slices (pastries), cocoa products, artificial coffee. On November 7, 2000, the registered owner name was approved to change to Chengdu Tongdefu. Various product packaging of Chengdu Tongdefu used phrases such as "Time-honored brand," "Century-old brand," and "Introduction of 'Tongdefu brand' peach slices: 'Tongdefu brand' peach slices were first made during the Qianlong reign of the Qing Dynasty (or 1840) with a long history and culture." On its website, the "Company Profile" page used the history of the Tongdefu Zhai Shop from the "Selected Historical Materials of Hechuan (Volume 2)" to promote its "Tongdefu" brand Hechuan peach slices.

On January 4, 2002, Yu Yongzuo's son Yu Xiaohua registered a sole proprietorship with the business name "Hechuan Time-honored Brand Tongdefu Peach Slice Factory," with business scope including self-produced peach slices and small snacks. In 2007, the business name was changed to "Chongqing Hechuan District Tongdefu Peach Slice Factory," which was later cancelled. On May 6, 2011, Chongqing Tongdefu was established with Yu Xiaohua as its legal representative, with business scope including pastry production. Chongqing Tongdefu is the owner of registered trademarks No. 6626473, a design mark with "Yu Fuguang 1898," and No. 7587928, a design mark with "Yu Xiaohua." Various product packaging of Chongqing Tongdefu used descriptions such as "Time-honored brand [Tongdefu] business name, founded in the 23rd year of the Guangxu reign of the Qing Dynasty (1898), with a long history" and information about awards received by the Tongdefu Zhai Shop, with some products adding "The above text is excerpted from the Hechuan County Annals" after such descriptions; "Ode to [Tongdefu]: Tongdefu, in Hechuan; well-known far and wide; for a hundred years; making peach slices; four generations passed down; high quality and fair price; honest and trustworthy; fair dealing; warm conversation"; "Hechuan peach slices"; "Chongqing Hechuan District Tongdefu Peach Slice Co., Ltd.," etc.

Judgment

The First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing rendered a civil judgment ( [2013] Yu Yi Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 00273 ) on July 3, 2013: 1. Chengdu Tongdefu shall immediately cease the false advertising acts in question. 2. Chengdu Tongdefu shall publish a statement on its website for five consecutive days after this judgment takes effect to eliminate the adverse effects caused by its false advertising. 3. All claims of Chengdu Tongdefu are dismissed. 4. The other counterclaims of Chongqing Tongdefu and Yu Xiaohua are dismissed. After the first instance judgment, Chengdu Tongdefu appealed. The Chongqing High People's Court rendered a civil judgment ( [2013] Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 00292 ) on December 17, 2013, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the sole proprietorship of Yu Xiaohua and Chongqing Tongdefu had similar business scope to Chengdu Tongdefu and thus had a competitive relationship. The inclusion of the word "Tongdefu" in their business names was identical to the word portion of Chengdu Tongdefu's registered trademark "Tongdefu TONGDEFU and device" and constituted similarity to that trademark. The key to determining whether the act of registering such business names constituted unfair competition was whether the act violated the principle of good faith. The evidence provided by Chengdu Tongdefu was insufficient to prove that the "Tongdefu TONGDEFU and device" trademark had become well-known to such an extent that others registering "Tongdefu" as a business name and using it in a standardized manner would cause public confusion. Therefore, it could not be established that Yu Xiaohua registered his sole proprietorship business name as "Tongdefu" with bad faith intent to free-ride. Moreover, during the period from the 1920s to the 1950s, the business name "Tongdefu" enjoyed high goodwill. The Tongdefu Zhai Shop was operated by three generations: Yu Hongchun, Yu Fuguang, and Yu Yongzuo. Particularly during Yu Fuguang's management, the peach slices produced by the shop received numerous honors. Yu Xiaohua, as the grandson of Yu Fuguang and son of Yu Yongzuo, had a reasonable basis for registering his sole proprietorship business name as "Tongdefu" based on the historical recognition of the Tongdefu Zhai Shop business name and his direct familial relationship with its operators. Yu Xiaohua's registration of the sole proprietorship business name was in good faith and did not violate the principle of good faith, thus not constituting unfair competition. Based on business continuity, his subsequent changes to the sole proprietorship business name and the registration of the company name of Chongqing Tongdefu also did not constitute unfair competition.

From the outer packaging of Chongqing Tongdefu's products, it used its full enterprise name, placed at the bottom of the front of the packaging. The three characters "Tongdefu" were part of the full enterprise name and were consistent with the overall presentation, without separate prominent use in abbreviated form or any special emphasis through changes in size, font, or color compared to other parts. Therefore, the placement of the enterprise name on the product packaging by Chongqing Tongdefu constituted standardized use, not prominent use of the business name, and did not constitute trademark infringement. Regarding the use of "Ode to Tongdefu" by Chongqing Tongdefu, the four characters "Ode to Tongdefu" were slightly larger than the specific content (a 36-character doggerel), but visually they formed a single whole. The specific content was an adaptation of similar text historically used by the Tongdefu Zhai Shop on its packaging, intended to indicate the history and business philosophy of the "Tongdefu" business name, not to prominently feature the word "Tongdefu." Moreover, the product packaging of Chongqing Tongdefu used multiple commercial identifiers, among which the collective mark "Hechuan Peach Slice" was particularly prominent, and its own trademark was also relatively noticeable. It also indicated the geographical indication "Hechuan Peach Slice" and recognition as a Chongqing municipal intangible cultural heritage. Compared with these identifiers, "Ode to Tongdefu" and its content were merely ordinary descriptive text, clearly not in the form of a commercial identifier and not sufficiently conspicuous. Objectively, they were unlikely to cause consumers to mistake the source of the products, nor did they function as a substitute for a trademark. Therefore, Chongqing Tongdefu's use of "Ode to Tongdefu" did not constitute "prominent use" in the sense of trademark infringement and did not constitute infringement of the trademark right.

The content on the website of Chengdu Tongdefu Company regarding the history and honors of the "Tongdefu Brand" peach slices was consistent with the historical records of the Tongdefu Zhai Shop, and the sources of the historical materials were indicated on its website. However, the company did not provide evidence to prove what connection it had with Tongdefu Zhai Shop. Furthermore, Chengdu Tongdefu Company also marked its product packaging with phrases such as "Century-old Brand," "Time-honored Brand," and "Founded during the Qianlong reign of the Qing Dynasty," whereas its "Tongdefu TONGDEFU and Device" trademark was approved for registration in 1998. The company also failed to provide evidence to support the basis for the above-mentioned markings. The aforementioned actions of Chengdu Tongdefu Company were inconsistent with the facts and easily misled consumers regarding the origin and history of its brand and its relationship with Tongdefu Zhai Shop, thereby gaining a competitive advantage. This constituted false advertising, and the company should bear the civil liability to cease the infringement and eliminate the adverse effects.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Li Jian, Zhou Lu, Song Lili)

**Guiding Case No. 59**

**Dai Shihua v. Jinan Municipal Public Security Fire Brigade — Dispute over Fire Protection Acceptance Inspection**

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on May 20, 2016)

**Keywords** Administrative litigation, Scope of acceptance, Administrative confirmation, Fire protection acceptance inspection, Record-filing result notice

**Ruling Gist**

Where a notice of the result of record-filing for fire protection acceptance inspection of a construction project contains an assessment of whether the fire protection completion acceptance is qualified, it has the nature of administrative confirmation. If a party files an administrative lawsuit against the act of issuing such a notice of record-filing result for fire protection acceptance inspection by a public security fire control institution, the people's court shall accept the case in accordance with the law.

**Related Legal Provisions**

Articles 4 and 13 of the Fire Control Law of the People's Republic of China

**Basic Facts**

The Plaintiff Dai Shihua alleged: The unit where the plaintiff resides has four households per floor on one stairway. The plaintiff's apartment, No. 801, faces east with its door opening outward. A fire hydrant measuring 1.6 meters high, 0.7 meters wide, and 0.25 meters thick is mounted on the south wall, 0.35 meters from the plaintiff's door. To enter, a person must step back to avoid the door, wait for it to open, and then move forward. The plaintiff cannot exit unless the door is opened 60 to 70 degrees. The installation and construction of the fire hydrant affect the plaintiff's daily life. The plaintiff requested the court to: annul the decision of the Defendant, the Jinan Municipal Public Security Fire Brigade, to approve the fire hydrant installed in front of his door as having passed the acceptance inspection; order the Defendant to instruct the project approval unit to rectify the issue within a specified period in accordance with national standards.

The Defendant, Jinan Municipal Public Security Fire Brigade, argued: The notice of the result of record-filing for fire protection acceptance inspection is a reflection of the inspection record completed in accordance with the evaluation standards for fire protection acceptance inspection of construction projects. If the record-filing result is qualified, it indicates that the construction project complies with relevant fire protection technical specifications; if unqualified, the public security fire control institution will take legal measures to require the construction unit to rectify the issues. Its nature is a technical acceptance inspection, not an independent and complete specific administrative act, and is not actionable. Therefore, it does not fall within the scope of acceptance of administrative cases in people's courts, and the plaintiff's lawsuit should be dismissed.

The court found through trial: For the renovation project of shantytown areas south of Guanyi Street (Buildings 1-8 and underground garage) where Dai Shihua resided, after randomly inspecting the fire protection facilities, the Jinan Municipal Public Security Fire Brigade issued the "Notice of Record-Filing Result for Fire Protection Completion Acceptance of Construction Project" (No. Jigong Xiaoyan Bei [2011] 0172) on November 21, 2011.

**Judgment**

The Jinan High-tech Industrial Development Zone People's Court rendered an administrative ruling on November 13, 2012 ((2012) Gao Xing Chu Zi No. 2), dismissing the plaintiff Dai Shihua's lawsuit. Dai Shihua appealed against the ruling of the first instance. The Jinan Intermediate People's Court, after trial, rendered an administrative ruling on January 17, 2013 ((2012) Ji Xing Zhong Zi No. 223): 1. Set aside the administrative ruling of the Jinan High-tech Industrial Development Zone People's Court ((2012) Gao Xing Chu Zi No. 2); 2. The case shall be continued for trial by the Jinan High-tech Industrial Development Zone People's Court.

**Reasoning**

The effective judgment of the court held: Regarding the nature of the act. Article 4 of the Fire Control Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Fire Control Law") provides: "The public security organs of local people's governments at or above the county level shall supervise and manage fire control work within their respective administrative regions, and the fire control institutions of the public security organs of the people's governments at the corresponding level shall be responsible for implementation." Article 3, Paragraph 2 of the Provisions of the Ministry of Public Security on the Supervision and Management of Fire Control in Construction Projects provides: "Public security fire control institutions shall, in accordance with the law, conduct fire protection design review, fire protection acceptance inspection, record-filing and random inspection of construction projects, and exercise fire protection supervision over construction projects." Article 24 provides: "For construction projects other than those specified in Articles 13 and 14 of these Provisions, the construction unit shall, within seven days from the date of obtaining the construction permit or the date of passing the completion acceptance of the project, conduct record-filing for fire protection design and fire protection completion acceptance through the website of the provincial public security fire control institution, or go to the business acceptance office of the public security fire control institution for such record-filing." The above provisions show that record-filing for fire protection acceptance inspection of a construction project is an act by a specific construction entity reporting the project's completion acceptance situation to the public security fire control institution, which registers and records it for inspection and supervision. The record-filing act is an act of the public security fire control institution exercising fire protection supervision and management over the construction project. The act of record-filing and random inspection of construction projects by fire control institutions bears the nature of exercising administrative powers, reflecting state will, legality, public interest, exclusivity, and compulsion. The notice of the record-filing result is a component of the record-filing act and a specific expression of the result of that act, and it also possesses the aforementioned characteristics of administrative powers; thus, it should fall within the scope of judicial review.

Regarding the consequences of the act. Article 13 of the Fire Control Law provides: "Upon completion of a construction project that requires fire protection design in accordance with the national fire protection technical standards for construction projects, fire protection acceptance inspection and record-filing shall be conducted according to the following provisions: ... (2) For other construction projects, the construction unit shall, after acceptance, report to the public security fire control institution for record-filing, and the public security fire control institution shall conduct random inspections. Construction projects that are legally required to undergo fire protection acceptance inspection shall not be put into use if they have not passed the fire protection acceptance inspection or if the inspection result is unqualified; other construction projects that are found to be unqualified through random inspections shall be stopped from use." Article 25 of the Ministry of Public Security's Provisions on the Supervision and Management of Fire Control in Construction Projects provides: "The public security fire control institution shall randomly determine inspection targets among the construction projects that have been filed for fire protection design and completion acceptance and shall make a public announcement. For those determined as inspection targets, the public security fire control institution shall, within twenty days, complete the inspection of drawings in accordance with fire protection laws and regulations and national fire protection technical standards for construction projects, or complete the project inspection in accordance with the evaluation standards for fire protection acceptance inspection of construction projects, and produce inspection records. The inspection results shall be made public. If the inspection result is unqualified, a written notice shall also be given to the construction unit. Upon receiving the notice, the construction unit shall stop construction or stop use, organize rectification, and then apply to the public security fire control institution for a re-inspection. The public security fire control institution shall, within twenty days from the date of receiving the written application, conduct a re-inspection and issue a written re-inspection opinion." The above provisions indicate that in the act of record-filing for completion acceptance, the public security fire control institution does not merely passively accept the relevant materials submitted by the construction unit; it also examines the recorded materials and completes the project inspection. The act of record-filing and random inspection of construction projects by the fire control institution can produce binding force under administrative law. For the construction unit, after the project's completion acceptance, it must file for record with the public security fire control institution; otherwise, it shall bear corresponding administrative liability. If the fire protection facilities are found to be unqualified through random inspection, they shall cease use, and rectification shall be organized. For the public security fire control institution, the record-filing result includes an assessment of whether the random inspection is qualified, which is essentially an act of administrative confirmation—an administrative act by which the public security fire control institution recognizes and confirms the legal facts and legal relations of the administrative counterpart. Once the fire protection facilities are assessed as qualified by the fire control institution, it is deemed that the fire control institution has factually confirmed that the fire protection project is qualified, and the relevant administrative counterpart will also be bound by this act.

Accordingly, the court held that the issuance of a notice of record-filing result for fire protection acceptance inspection of a construction project is the final step in the supervision and management of the quality of fire protection facilities in the construction project. The notice of record-filing result contains an assessment of whether the fire protection completion acceptance is qualified, has the nature of administrative confirmation, and is a specific administrative act taken by the public security fire control institution. The completion of the record-filing procedure can produce binding force under administrative law. Therefore, the record-filing act is an actionable administrative act, and the people's court can conduct judicial review of it. The original ruling, which held that the notice of the record-filing result for fire protection acceptance inspection of a construction project was a technical acceptance inspection notice, not a specific administrative act, and accordingly dismissed the lawsuit of the appellant Dai Shihua, was indeed improper.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Zhang Jifeng, Sun Jifa, Shan Lei)

**Guiding Case No. 60**

**Yancheng Aokang Food Co., Ltd. Dongtai Branch v. Yancheng Dongtai Administration for Industry and Commerce — Dispute over Administrative Penalty for Violation of Food Safety Standards**

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on May 20, 2016)

**Keywords** Administrative, Administrative penalty, Food safety standards, Food labels, Food instructions

**Ruling Gist**

1. Where a food business operator, on a food label or in food instructions, particularly emphasizes the addition or inclusion of one or more valuable or distinctive ingredients or components, it shall indicate the amount or content of the emphasized ingredient or component added. If it fails to do so, this constitutes a violation of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China. If the administrative department for industry and commerce imposes an administrative penalty on the operator in accordance with the law, the people's court shall uphold it.

2. The term "emphasis" refers to prominent identification through means such as names, color differences, fonts, font sizes, graphics, arrangement order, textual descriptions, repeated appearance of the same content, or multiple contents pointing to the same thing. The term "valuable or distinctive ingredients" refers to special ingredients different from ordinary ingredients, having higher nutritional value for the human body, and their market prices and nutritional content are often higher than those of other ingredients.

**Related Legal Provisions**

Article 20 and Article 42, Paragraph 1 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (This Law was revised on April 24, 2015; the corresponding articles in the new Law are Article 26 and Article 67, Paragraph 1).

**Basic Facts**

The Plaintiff, Yancheng Aokang Food Co., Ltd. Dongtai Branch (hereinafter "Aokang Company"), alleged: On May 15, 2012, the Defendant, Yancheng Dongtai Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter "Dongtai AIC"), issued an "Administrative Penalty Decision" (Dong Gong Shang An Zi [2012] No. 00298), finding that the plaintiff's sale of Jinlongyu Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil failed to indicate the content of olive oil, violating the provisions of GB7718-2004 "General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods," and ordered the plaintiff to correct the violation and imposed a total forfeiture and fine of RMB 60,000. The plaintiff argued that the term "Olive Original Fragrance" on the label of the Jinlongyu Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil it sold was an objective description of the product's physical attributes, not an emphasis on a particular ingredient, and thus did not require indication of content or amount added. Olive oil is an ordinary edible oil ingredient, similar to other ingredients such as rapeseed oil and soybean oil, without special effects or value, and is not a "valuable or distinctive ingredient." This case should be governed by the national food safety standards promulgated by the health administrative department of the State Council under the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Food Safety Law"). The standard GB7718-2004 "General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods" applied by the defendant is not a national food safety standard, constituting an erroneous application of law. In summary, the plaintiff requested the court to annul the administrative penalty decision in question.

The Defendant Dongtai AIC argued: The front label of the Jinlongyu brand Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil sold by the plaintiff Aokang Company prominently featured the character "olive" with an olive graphic, and the hangtag stated "Added 100% extra virgin olive oil from Italy," but the amount added was not indicated. This constitutes a situation where a food label particularly emphasizes the addition of a valuable or distinctive ingredient without indicating the amount added. GB7718-2004 "General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods," as a mandatory standard for food labeling, is deemed one of the food safety standards after the Food Safety Law came into effect, until it was replaced by GB7718-2011 "General Standard for the Management of Prepackaged Food Labeling." Therefore, its administrative penalty decision was accurate in characterization, reasonable and appropriate, and procedurally lawful, and the defendant requested the court to uphold it.

The court found through trial: From September 1, 2011, to February 29, 2012, Aokang Company purchased 290 bottles of Jinlongyu brand Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil (net content 5 liters) and sold them at a markup to Qianjiahui Supermarket, achieving sales revenue of RMB 34,800 and net profit of RMB 2,836.9. On February 21, 2012, during an inspection at Qianjiahui Supermarket, law enforcement officers of Dongtai AIC discovered that the above-mentioned Jinlongyu brand Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil did not indicate the amount of olive oil added. The product name was "Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil." Its label featured the characters "olive" and an olive graphic. The side of the label indicated "Ingredients: Rapeseed Oil, Soybean Oil, Olive Oil," and the hangtag stated: "Jinlongyu Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil, added with 100% extra virgin olive oil from Italy, exudes a faint olive fruit fragrance. In addition to being rich in various vitamins, monounsaturated fatty acids, and other healthy substances, its olive essence contains natural antioxidant components such as polyphenols, satisfying the pursuit of natural, healthy, high-quality life."

Dongtai AIC initiated an investigation on February 27, 2012, and served a notice of hearing for administrative penalty on the plaintiff Aokang Company on May 9. The plaintiff did not make any statements or defenses within the statutory period, nor did it request a hearing. On May 15, the defendant served the Administrative Penalty Decision (Dong Gong Shang An Zi [2012] No. 298) on the plaintiff, finding that the plaintiff operated food with labels that did not comply with the Food Safety Law, specifically by particularly emphasizing the addition of a valuable or distinctive ingredient without indicating the amount added on the food label. Pursuant to the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China and the Food Safety Law, the defendant ordered the plaintiff to correct the violation, confiscated illegal gains of RMB 2,836.9, and imposed a fine of RMB 57,163.1, totaling RMB 60,000 in forfeiture and fine. The plaintiff, dissatisfied, applied for administrative reconsideration, and the Yancheng Administration for Industry and Commerce upheld the penalty decision.

**Judgment**

The Dongtai People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered an administrative judgment on December 15, 2012 ((2012) Dong Xing Chu Zi No. 0068), upholding the Administrative Penalty Decision (Dong Gong Shang An Zi [2012] No. 00298) issued by Dongtai AIC on May 15, 2012. After the judgment was pronounced, Aokang Company appealed to the Yancheng Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province. The Yancheng Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered an administrative judgment on May 9, 2013 ((2013) Yan Xing Zhong Zi No. 0032), affirming the first-instance judgment.

**Reasoning**

The effective judgment of the court held: Article 20, Item 4 of the Food Safety Law provides that food safety standards shall include requirements for labels, markings, and instructions related to food safety and nutrition. Article 22 provides that before the national food safety standards specified in this Law are announced, food producers and business operators shall produce and operate food in accordance with the current edible agricultural product quality and safety standards, food hygiene standards, food quality standards, and relevant industry standards for food. GB7718-2004 "General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods" was formulated by the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine and the Standardization Administration of China and came into effect on October 1, 2005. The Food Safety Law came into effect on June 1, 2009. The new version, GB7718-2011 "General Standard for the Management of Prepackaged Food Labeling," was formulated by the health administrative department of the State Council, explicitly as a national food safety standard, and came into effect on April 20, 2012. In this case, the plaintiff Aokang Company's illegal act occurred between September 2011 and February 2012. GB7718-2004 "General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods" was one of the national food safety standards at that time. Therefore, the defendant Dongtai AIC's application of GB7718-2004 to impose the administrative penalty on the plaintiff was not improper.

GB7718-2004 "General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods" provides: "All content on the label of prepackaged foods shall not introduce the food through false, misleading, or deceptive text, graphics, or other means; nor shall it mislead consumers through font size or color differences." "If the food label or food instructions particularly emphasize the addition of one or more valuable or distinctive ingredients, the amount of the emphasized ingredient added shall be indicated." The term "emphasis" here refers to giving special emphasis or prominence. Generally, it can be understood as emphasizing something through means such as names, color differences, fonts, font sizes, graphics, arrangement order, textual descriptions, repeated appearance of the same content, or multiple contents pointing to the same thing. "Valuable or distinctive ingredients" refer to special ingredients that have higher nutritional value for the human body and are different from ordinary ingredients. Typically, the market price or nutritional content of such ingredients is higher than that of other ingredients. In this case, the plaintiff Aokang Company argued that "Olive Original Fragrance" was an objective description of the product's physical attributes, not an emphasis on a particular ingredient. However, looking at the external packaging of the Jinlongyu brand Olive Original Fragrance Edible Blended Oil sold by the plaintiff, its label prominently highlighted the character "olive" through graphics, fonts, and textual descriptions, emphasizing that the edible blended oil contained olive oil as an ingredient. Furthermore, the hangtag (part of the food label) contained textual statements such as "Added 100% extra virgin olive oil from Italy," which obviously emphasized to consumers that the product contained olive oil as an ingredient. This practice itself indeed emphasized the value and distinctiveness of "olive" in the product. Generally, the market price or nutritional value of olive oil is higher than that of ordinary soybean oil, rapeseed oil, etc. Therefore, if olive oil is added to edible blended oil, it can be determined that olive oil is a "valuable or distinctive ingredient." Consequently, Aokang Company's failure to indicate the amount of olive oil added constituted a violation of food safety standards. The administrative penalty decision made by Dongtai AIC was based on facts and law and should be upheld.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Liu Hong, Wang Weihua, Zhou He)
